security_spec.violation_condition: When Sscofpmf hardware is present (has_sscofpmf=1), the FreeBSD kernel never writes scounteren or mcounteren to enable HPM-counter access from S-mode, never saves/restores hpmcounter/mhpmevent state across context switches in swtch.S, and has no trap handler for the count-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) if delegated to S-mode via mideleg — counter state from M-mode firmware (OpenSBI) or prior kernel operations persists unswitched across thread boundaries, and an undelivered LCOFI interrupt may cause an unhandled-trap panic.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: swtch.S context-switch path missing hpmcounter/mhpmevent save/restore; no csr_write(scounteren, *) in kernel; no LCOFI trap handler registered; has_sscofpmf checked but never acted upon
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD detects Sscofpmf but never manages HPM counter state — swtch.S leaks counter values across threads, scounteren stays zero blocking legitimate access, and no LCOFI handler exists, violating thread-isolation invariants when M-mode firmware has counters running

findings.finding: has_sscofpmf is declared as a global flag but never read by any kernel code. The CPU announces Sscofpmf support (detected via ISA string parsing at line 467), but the kernel takes zero action — no scounteren init, no context-switch hooks, no LCOFI handler registration. Dead-capability flag.

cpu_switch() saves/restores only GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11) and optionally FPU state. No hpmcounter3–31 or mhpmevent3–31 CSR save/restore exists anywhere in the context-switch path. When M-mode firmware has configured mcounteren to grant S-mode HPM access, the 29 counter CSRs and their event-selector CSRs carry stale values from the previous thread into the next — a cross-thread information leak through performance-monitor state.
findings.snippet:
sd  ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
sd  sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
sd  s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)
...
sd  s11, (PCB_S + 11 * 8)(x13)

findings.finding: cpu_throw() — the fast-path context switch for a new thread — likewise only restores GPRs and optionally FPU state. No hpmcounter/mhpmevent save/restore. The new thread inherits whatever HPM counter values the previous thread (or M-mode firmware) left in hardware.
findings.snippet:
ld  ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
ld  sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
ld  s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)
...
ld  s11, (PCB_S + 11 * 8)(x13)

findings.finding: The trap-entry save_registers macro saves all GPRs plus sepc, sstatus, stval, scause — but does not read or snapshot scounteren or any hpmcounter CSR. If the kernel ever uses HPM counters for profiling, trap entries will corrupt counter values (e.g., counting trap-handling instructions as user/kernel work). This is currently latent since hwpmc is disabled on RISC-V.
findings.snippet:
csrr  t0, sepc
sd    t0, (TF_SEPC)(sp)
csrr  t0, sstatus
sd    t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
csrr  t0, stval
sd    t0, (TF_STVAL)(sp)
csrr  t0, scause
sd    t0, (TF_SCAUSE)(sp)

findings.finding: do_trap_supervisor() switch on scause has a default case that panics. If M-mode firmware sets mideleg[13] to delegate the local-counter-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) to S-mode, the kernel receives scause=0x800000000000000d (interrupt bit | 13). SCAUSE_CODE masks this to 13, which matches no case label, falls to default, and triggers panic("Unknown kernel exception") — a guaranteed denial-of-service on counter overflow.

ditto for do_trap_user(): LCOFI (interrupt 13) falls to default → panic. If LCOFI fires while in U-mode and is delegated to S-mode by mideleg, the kernel panics identically. No graceful signal delivery (SIGEMT or similar) exists.

The IRQ enum defines slots for software (bits 0–3), timer (bits 4–7), and external (bits 8–11) interrupts, but no IRQ_COUNT_OVERFLOW entry for bit 13. Without this enum value, no interrupt handler can be registered for LCOFI even if kernel code wanted to.

MIP, MIE, SIP, and SIE bit definitions cover bits 0–12 but stop before bit 13 (LCOFI). MIP_LCOFIP, SIP_LCOFIP, MIE_LCOFIE, and SIE_LCOFIE are all absent. The kernel cannot mask, check, or acknowledge the count-overflow interrupt via the standard interrupt-pending/enable CSRs.
findings.snippet:
MIE_MTIE  (1 << 7)   /* last MIE bit defined */
MIP_MTIP  (1 << 7)   /* last MIP bit defined */
SIE_SEIE  (1 << 9)   /* last SIE bit defined */
/* bit 13 LCOFI: undefined */

findings.finding: The boot sequence sets stvec and sscratch, then jumps to initriscv() → mi_startup without writing scounteren. The scounteren CSR remains at its reset value (likely 0, blocking all U-mode HPM-counter access). While this prevents user info leaks, it also means the kernel has no deliberate policy for scounteren — it passively inherits whatever M-mode left, and adds no initialization.
findings.snippet:
la   t0, cpu_exception_handler
csrw stvec, t0
li   t0, 0
csrw sscratch, t0
...
call _C_LABEL(initriscv)
call _C_LABEL(mi_startup)

findings.finding: initriscv() calls identify_cpu() which sets has_sscofpmf=1 when the ISA string includes 'sscofpmf', but then proceeds through pmap_bootstrap, cninit, init_proc0, mutex_init, etc. without ever writing scounteren or initializing HPM counter state. The entire boot path has no Sscofpmf-aware initialization.

CSR_SCOUNTEREN (0x106) and CSR_MCOUNTEREN (0x306) are defined with DECLARE_CSR macros, making csr_read(scounteren, ...) / csr_write(scounteren, ...) syntactically valid. However, the Sscofpmf-spec SCOUNTOVF CSR (0xda0) is not defined anywhere in encoding.h, so even a correctly-implemented handler could not poll overflow status via the standard csr_read interface.
